title: The Brew Shop - Weekly Email Update
contentHtml:
Hey Brew Shop Fam!
Here's an update of what's happening this week - from new beer drops, wine reviews, our current tap list, to upcoming tastings, and more. 

SHOP THIS WEEK’S NEWSLETTER HERE SHOP OUR ENTIRE STOCK OF BEER, WINE & HOMEBREW HERE

Join us this Friday from 5-7 PM as we welcome Ben from Right Proper for our free tasting! Scroll down to the bottom of our newsletter to see the full line-up for September!

Benito Santos Saiar Albarino: In my CPA days when I was under pressure to pick a bottle from the wine list, I'd often choose Albariño both as a wild card and equalizer for competing tastes. Saiar Albariño was love at first sniff for me (and apparently many of our Wine Club members who have been special ordering this bottle since we featured it earlier this year!). With aromatics of peach and white flowers, the wine transports you to the coast with a saltiness and minerality paired with citrus and tropical fruit.

Domaine du Salvard Cheverny Blanc: This fresh, elegant white from France’s Loire Valley combines bright citrus, grapefruit and floral notes with a subtle roundness and texture, finishing with refreshing acidity and a touch of minerality. It’s an especially versatile wine to enjoy alongside seafood, grilled fish, asparagus, and goat cheese.

Henri Perrusset Macon-Villages:This Burgundy Chardonnay is a crowd-pleaser. It spends 8-10 months on the lees in stainless steel to give it that beautifully balanced creaminess and acidity. Think ripe pear, stone fruit, and citrus, with a touch of minerality. Pair this with brunch foods, seafood, you name it.

Benoit et Mathieu Fleuriet Sancerre Magie des Caillotte Renaissance: Renaissance is a collaboration between friends (insert heart hands). "Magie des Caillottes" is named after Sancerre's caillottes soil — the stony, calcareous limestone that works absolute magic on Sauvignon Blanc. Lively and razor-sharp with zesty citrus, green apple and plenty of wet limestone minerality. Organic, Biodynamic & Hand Harvested

Qupe Chardonnay: Qupe is known for sourcing some of the best cool climate Chardonnay on the Central Coast. This yields wonderfully intense fruit, but perfectly balanced acidity. Everything you want in a CA Chard, Qupe strikes great balance between creaminess and toast, for a rich and decadent Chardonnay with pops of stone fruit, white flowers, brioche, and vanilla.

Mary Taylor Costieres de Nimes Caroline Pozzo di Borgo: A Grenache heavy French blend is a fan favorite here at The Brew Shop and Caroline Pozzo di Borgo delivers with this certified organic beauty. Juicy, fresh red fruit and lilac meet earthiness, pillowy tannins, and that gorgeous quintessential French mustiness.

Bodegas Ochoa Labrit Garnacha: Sisters Adriana and Beatriz run the show at Bodegas Ochoa — with Adriana having been named Best Young Female Winemaker in Spain. Labrit Garnacha is wonderfully nerdy with Adriana sourcing the grapes from organic vineyards planted with 200 recovered biotypes of ancestral Garnacha, painstakingly identified and preserved by the Public University of Navarra. Aged in a combo of concrete and French oak, Labrit Garnacha smells like the very best blackberry and raspberry compote. On the palate, enjoy juicy red fruits mingling with herbs and cocoa.

Paolo Conterno Barolo Riva del Bric: The Conterno family has been making Barolo for four generations on the famous Ginestra vineyard, which is widely considered one of the best single vineyards in the entire Barolo appellation. Coming from 25 year old vines at over 300 meters in elevation. Riva del Bric Barolo is serious, but also seriously drinkable. A gorgeous garnet wine with fresh roses, dried earth and herbs on the nose with wild cherry, dark currant, and a mysterious hint of rusty nail and shaved pencil that sounds alarming but is actually completely mesmerizing.

You know we are always on the hunt for what I'll call "value wine": wine that is both good quality and affordable. In the deep well of history here at The Brew Shop sometimes patterns emerge in this hunt. One that we've seen a few times and that we're always happy to see again is the gorgeous French blend of Colombard and Ugni Blanc.

Les Parcellaires de l'Herré is 75% Colombard and 25% Ugni Blanc, aka Trebbiano. Both grapes make for an aromatic, crisp wine that's fresh and lively with high acidity. Domaine de l'Herre does exactly that with Les Parcellaires. Fresh citrus and tropical fruit pop with zesty acidity and some lovely floral undertones. It's a great pairer for your patio or balcony, whether you're snacking away out there or eating nothing at all. Most importantly, this bottle is a crusher and sitting at only $13.99 on the shelf. And yes, that's a flying rhino on the front of the bottle and yes, it's somehow very endearing.

This week’s writeup is brought to you by Julie

Thanks for your business! See you soon, Beth, Julie & Aidan and the entire Brew Crew
